However after the Uprising of 1811 Egypt retook the city from the Christian rebels, and have refused to return the land to us. They have now replied to our latest demand for its return with a total refusal. They say that the city was lost to rebels during our rule, and that a city such as Jerusalem needs stability to ensure the safe passage of those who go there on pilgrimages. This goes against the word of the Caliph, and is treason of the highest order. §!The City of Jerusalem, being the third holiest city in Islam, should reasonably be held by the stewards of the faith. They have now replied to our latest demand for its return with a proposal. They will be allowed to keep the lands of Jerusalem and Transjordan, and in return they will come to the aid of the Sultan Mehmed II of Rum in the war against Cappadocia. §REnsuring the victory of Rum is vital for Muslim control over Anatolia, yet we would have to give up our claim on Jerusalem to guarantee it. Rum might very well win the war without the help of Egypt, but knowing that we intervened on their behalf would surely help ensure the continued loyalty of the Sultanate.§!§g

§!The City of Jerusalem, being the third holiest city in Islam, should reasonably be held by the stewards of the faith. However after the Uprising of 1811 Egypt retook the city from the Christian rebels, and have refused to return the land to us. They have now replied to our latest demand with an explanation, stating that they have now ensured the region will remain stable under our control and that it will be returned with haste. The Caliph's word carries immense power, so it does not take much genius to understand that they are most likely trying to gain favor with the Caliph. Regardless of their intent, they have today shown themselves to be loyal servants, and we will of course always value those that are loyal to the true Caliph.§g
§!The Sultan of Rum has responded to our proposal. He has agreed to our demands and will now serve as our loyal governor of Anatolia.§g
